title: Where does the Sun rise in June?
hook: The Sun rises in the east. In London in June, does it?

knows: that the Sun rises in the east and sets in the west
doesNotKnow: how far from east the Sun rises at high latitudes
that the rise point moves with the seasons

misconception: The Sun always rises due east and sets due west.
objective: The learner can say that at London the Sun rises about north-east (50°) in June, south-east (130°) in December and due east only at the equinoxes, a swing of about 80°.

claims.text: At latitude 51.5°N, the Sun's rise bearing A from north satisfies cos A = sin(declination) / cos(latitude); it sets at 360° - A.
claims.source: Spherical astronomy (e.g. Meeus, Astronomical Algorithms, ch. 15) for a flat geometric horizon: the Sun is on the horizon when its altitude is 0. From memory of the textbook, not re-checked. The set bearing is the mirror image.

claims.text: On 21 June the Sun rises at about 50° (north-east); on 21 December at about 130° (south-east); at the equinox at 90°.
claims.source: Builder's node check for latitude 51.5072: declination 23.44 gives 50.28; -23.44 gives 129.72; 0 gives 90.00. Dates use a circular-orbit model: declination = asin(sin 23.44 deg x sin(360 (day - 80)/365.25)), day 172 = 21 June, 355 = 21 December, 80 = 21 March; real solstice/equinox dates vary by a day.

claims.text: The Sun's rise point swings about 80° between June and December at London's latitude.
claims.source: 129.72 - 50.28 = 79.44 degrees; the reveal rounds it to 79 (computed in code from the same function).

claims.text: The Sun rises due east only when day and night are equal, in March and September.
claims.source: cos A = 0 requires declination 0, which occurs at the equinoxes (when day and night are about equal; on a flat geometric horizon exactly equal). Refraction makes real day slightly longer; stated loosely.

claims.text: Air bends the light by under 1°, which changes the sunrise bearing little.
claims.source: From the brief (cm-geography), citing Meeus: refraction changes the rise bearing by under 1 degree at this latitude. Not independently checked by the builder.

claims.text: London is at 51.5°N and the Sun's maximum declination is 23.44°.
claims.source: From memory, not re-checked: London 51.5072 N; axial tilt 23.44 degrees (IAU/Astronomical Almanac, slowly changing).

claims.text: The Sun rises in the east.
claims.source: Hook: the everyday statement the lesson tests (true on average and at the equinoxes).

claims.text: The stage is a toy: a flat horizon seen from above, no air.
claims.source: Model label on the stage; geometry only.

recall.question: In London in June, the Sun rises in which direction?
recall.why: In summer the Sun is north of the celestial equator, so at 51.5°N it rises about north-east (50°) and sets north-west.
